source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Dusko, when I opened the integrated board the 3D viewer was missing a few components because some 3D models point to libraries that only exist on your machine. Could you send me these three files?

USB4215-03-A.stp (from your Vucko.3dshapes) — for USB1
Q\_SOT-23.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for Q3
TS-1088-AR02016.step (from the JLCPCB plugin library) — for S1

Once I have them I'll drop them into the project's libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/ folder. Thanks!

value_updates.model_file_packaging: Include required 3D model files in the project rather than depending on libraries available only on the designer's machine.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Also FYI when I opened the integrated board on my Linux machine I noticed the project had a few absolute Windows paths and references to libraries you have locally but I don't, so most components weren't showing in the 3D viewer. I patched it up on my side. 12 hard-coded Windows paths like D:/KiCAD Projekti/Upwork/Amir Cicak/Radni/IoT\_Environmental\_Monitoring\_Device\_All/libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/... — I replaced them with ${KIPRJMOD}/libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/... (relative). The files themselves are in libs/ so this works on any machine.

I can do this it is not a problem for me but just wanted to let you know.

value_updates.model_reference_path_policy: Use project-relative ${KIPRJMOD}/libs/easyeda/easyeda.3dshapes/... references instead of absolute machine-specific paths.

source_message.text: Yeah, Also ${KICAD8\_3RD\_PARTY} is a KiCad 8 path variable — KiCad 9 uses ${KICAD9\_3RD\_PARTY} — so even on a machine where the JLCPCB plugin is installed, those refs would break in KiCad 9.

value_updates.kicad_version_compatibility: 3D model references must work in KiCad 9 and must not rely on the KiCad 8-only ${KICAD8_3RD_PARTY} variable.
